newsitem.title: USA: Safeway to consider expanding repurchase.
newsitem.headline: Safeway to consider expanding repurchase.

text.p: Safeway Inc will look favorably on expanding its stock repurchase program after it completes a 15 million share buyback from partnerships controlled by affiliates of Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co, Safeway Chief Executive Officer Steven Burd said Monday.
A Safeway spokesman said Burd, who was speaking on a conference call, was referring to opportunities when KKR partners may seek liquidity on their holdings.
Vons Cos Inc Chief Executive Officer Lawrence Del Santo, speaking on the same conference call, said he plans to retire by the second quarter of 1997.
A Vons-Safeway merger, announced earlier today, is expected to be completed by late March or early April, a Safeway spokesman said.
Burd said he did not expect major layoffs to result from the merger. "I think it's fair to say that there is some overlap, but cost savings (from elimination of redundancies) are small," he said.

Safeway is to issue 1.425 shares for each Vons shares it does not already own, up from 1.34 shares offered on October 30. While the ratio is higher, the dollar value has decreased due to a decline Safeway's share price.
"Our share price has been under tremendous pressure from arbitrageurs, but what Vons holders are getting is the value of the combined companies," Burd said.
